column3: Insomnia, to be unable to sleep: 我失眠了 "I couldn't sleep", 长期失眠 "long-term insomnia", 失眠的人. 失 "lose" + 眠 "sleep". It is the plain verb and noun for a poor night's sleep that comes from worry or stress.
column4: 他最近压力大，常常失眠。
column5: 他最近壓力大，常常失眠。
column6: Tā zuìjìn yālì dà, chángcháng shīmián.
column7: He is under a lot of stress lately and often can't sleep.
column9: Insomnia, to be unable to sleep: 我失眠了 "I couldn't sleep", 長期失眠 "long-term insomnia", 失眠的人. 失 "lose" + 眠 "sleep". It is the plain verb and noun for a poor night's sleep that comes from worry or stress.

column3: City resident, citizen: 市民大会, 台北市民, 市民专线 "city hotline". 市 "city" + 民 "people". It means the people of a city as members of a community with rights and duties. For the country, the word is 国民 or 公民.
column4: 市政府请市民节约用水。
column5: 市政府請市民節約用水。
column6: Shìzhèngfǔ qǐng shìmín jiéyuē yòngshuǐ.
column7: The city government asks residents to save water.
column9: City resident, citizen: 市民大會, 台北市民, 市民專線 "city hotline". 市 "city" + 民 "people". It means the people of a city as members of a community with rights and duties. For the country, the word is 國民 or 公民.

column3: Teacher's wife: a respectful address for the wife of your teacher or master: 师母好. 师 "teacher" + 母 "mother". It is used in a school of martial arts, music or calligraphy, and for any teacher you owe a lot to.
column4: 每次去老师家，师母都准备很多好吃的。
column5: 每次去老師家，師母都準備很多好吃的。
column6: Měi cì qù lǎoshī jiā, shīmǔ dōu zhǔnbèi hěn duō hǎochī de.
column7: Every time we visit the teacher's home, his wife has prepared lots of good food.
column9: Teacher's wife: a respectful address for the wife of your teacher or master: 師母好. 師 "teacher" + 母 "mother". It is used in a school of martial arts, music or calligraphy, and for any teacher you owe a lot to.

column3: Period, phase of time: 学生时期 "student days", 特殊时期 "a special period", 战争时期 "wartime", 青春期. The period is a stretch with its own features, a few years or a few decades. 时 "time" + 期 "a set period". It is not for a point in time, which is 时候.
column4: 这是我人生最快乐的时期。
column5: 這是我人生最快樂的時期。
column6: Zhè shì wǒ rénshēng zuì kuàilè de shíqī.
column7: This is the happiest period of my life.
column9: Period, phase of time: 學生時期 "student days", 特殊時期 "a special period", 戰爭時期 "wartime", 青春期. The period is a stretch with its own features, a few years or a few decades. 時 "time" + 期 "a set period". It is not for a point in time, which is 時候.

column3: Often, constantly: 时时提醒 "remind constantly", 时时刻刻 "every moment", 时时注意. It is written style, and the doubled form means "at all times", more than 常常. Often paired with 刻刻 in the set phrase. In speech 常常 or 一直 is more natural.
column6: Wǒmen yào shíshí zhùyì ānquán.
column7: We must pay attention to safety at all times.
column9: Often, constantly: 時時提醒 "remind constantly", 時時刻刻 "every moment", 時時注意. It is written style, and the doubled form means "at all times", more than 常常. Often paired with 刻刻 in the set phrase. In speech 常常 or 一直 is more natural.

column3: To demonstrate, to protest: 示威游行 "a protest march", 示威抗议, 人民示威. 示 "show" + 威 "power, might", showing strength or feeling. It can also be a show of military strength.
column6: Mínzhòng zài jiētóu shìwēi.
column7: People are demonstrating in the street.
column9: To demonstrate, to protest: 示威遊行 "a protest march", 示威抗議, 人民示威. 示 "show" + 威 "power, might", showing strength or feeling. It can also be a show of military strength.

column3: Style, design, pattern: 式样新颖 "new in style", 各种式样 "all sorts of styles", 衣服的式样. It speaks of the look or cut of a clothes, furniture or building. 式 "form" + 样 "appearance". In shops 款式 is the more common word, with 式样 a bit more formal.
column4: 这家店的鞋子式样很多。
column5: 這家店的鞋子式樣很多。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de xiézi shìyàng hěn duō.
column7: This shop has shoes in many styles.
column9: Style, design, pattern: 式樣新穎 "new in style", 各種式樣 "all sorts of styles", 衣服的式樣. It speaks of the look or cut of a clothes, furniture or building. 式 "form" + 樣 "appearance". In shops 款式 is the more common word, with 式樣 a bit more formal.

column3: Field of view, vision: 视野开阔 "a wide view", 扩大视野 "broaden one's horizons", 窗外的视野. It is a view as the eye takes it in, and a view of the mind: 国际视野. 视 "look" + 野 "open country". Travel and study are said to widen it.
column4: 出国旅行可以开阔视野。
column5: 出國旅行可以開闊視野。
column6: Chūguó lǚxíng kěyǐ kāikuò shìyě.
column7: Traveling abroad can broaden your horizons.
column9: Field of view, vision: 視野開闊 "a wide view", 擴大視野 "broaden one's horizons", 窗外的視野. It is a view as the eye takes it in, and a view of the mind: 國際視野. 視 "look" + 野 "open country". Travel and study are said to widen it.

column3: To sell: a bound form: 出售 "for sale", 售价 "price", 售货员 "salesclerk", 售票 "sell tickets", 零售 "retail", 销售 "sales". On signs: 售完 "sold out", 售票处 "ticket office". In speech 卖 is used. The character is a bird 隹 over a mouth 口, a seller calling out his goods.
column6: Zhè běn shū yǐjīng shòuwán le.
column7: This book is sold out.
column9: To sell: a bound form: 出售 "for sale", 售價 "price", 售貨員 "salesclerk", 售票 "sell tickets", 零售 "retail", 銷售 "sales". On signs: 售完 "sold out", 售票處 "ticket office". In speech 賣 is used. The character is a bird 隹 over a mouth 口, a seller calling out his goods.

column3: Flashlight: 一支手电筒, 用手电筒照, 手电筒没电了. The measure is 支 or 把. 手 "hand" + 电 "electric" + 筒 "tube", an electric tube you hold. 筒 has 竹 "bamboo" above, since the first tubes were bamboo.
column6: Tíngdiàn le, kuài ná shǒudiàntǒng lái.
column7: The power's out, quickly bring the flashlight.
column9: Flashlight: 一支手電筒, 用手電筒照, 手電筒沒電了. The measure is 支 or 把. 手 "hand" + 電 "electric" + 筒 "tube", an electric tube you hold. 筒 has 竹 "bamboo" above, since the first tubes were bamboo.

column3: Receipt: 开收据 "issue a receipt", 保留收据, 一张收据. In Taiwan, a receipt from a shop can be 收据 or 发票 (which is the official uniform invoice that also has a lottery number). 收 "receive" + 据 "evidence, proof". 收据 proves that money or goods were received.
column6: Qǐng bǎoliú shōujù, yǐbiàn tuìhuò.
column7: Please keep the receipt in case you return the goods.
column9: Receipt: 開收據 "issue a receipt", 保留收據, 一張收據. In Taiwan, a receipt from a shop can be 收據 or 發票 (which is the official uniform invoice that also has a lottery number). 收 "receive" + 據 "evidence, proof". 收據 proves that money or goods were received.

column3: Life span: 平均寿命 "average life expectancy", 寿命很长, 电池的寿命 "battery life". It is for people, animals and machines, as the time something lives or works. 寿 "longevity" + 命 "life". For birthdays 寿 appears also in 寿星 "the birthday person".
column4: 台湾人的平均寿命越来越长。
column5: 臺灣人的平均壽命越來越長。
column6: Táiwānrén de píngjūn shòumìng yuèláiyuè cháng.
column7: The average life span of people in Taiwan keeps getting longer.
column9: Life span: 平均壽命 "average life expectancy", 壽命很長, 電池的壽命 "battery life". It is for people, animals and machines, as the time something lives or works. 壽 "longevity" + 命 "life". For birthdays 壽 appears also in 壽星 "the birthday person".

column3: Number, figure, and "several": 数字 "digit", 数量 "quantity", 人数 "number of people", 数学 "math", 数十年 "several decades". It is read shù for these, while the verb "to count" is shǔ (数一数). In the first senses it is mostly met in compounds. The right half 攵 stands for an old "strike" part and 娄 gives the sound (lóu, no longer close).
column6: Zhèlǐ de xuéshēng shùliàng bù duō.
column7: There are not many students here.
column9: Number, figure, and "several": 數字 "digit", 數量 "quantity", 人數 "number of people", 數學 "math", 數十年 "several decades". It is read shù for these, while the verb "to count" is shǔ (數一數). In the first senses it is mostly met in compounds. The right half 攵 stands for an old "strike" part and 婁 gives the sound (lóu, no longer close).

column3: Rat, mouse: 一只老鼠, 捉老鼠, 老鼠药. It covers both words in English. The computer mouse is 滑鼠 in Taiwan and 鼠标 on the mainland. 老 is only a prefix here, with no sense of "old", and 鼠 is the animal itself; 鼠 stands alone for the year of the Rat in the zodiac. The classifier is 只.
column6: Chúfáng lǐ yǒu yī zhī lǎoshǔ.
column7: There is a mouse in the kitchen.
column9: Rat, mouse: 一隻老鼠, 捉老鼠, 老鼠藥. It covers both words in English. The computer mouse is 滑鼠 in Taiwan and 鼠標 on the mainland. 老 is only a prefix here, with no sense of "old", and 鼠 is the animal itself; 鼠 stands alone for the year of the Rat in the zodiac. The classifier is 隻.

column3: To play with, to wield, to show off: 耍花招 "play tricks", 耍脾气 "throw a tantrum", 耍帅 "show off, act cool", 耍宝 "clown around". It is a spoken word with a feel of playing with or putting on a performance. 耍嘴皮子 is "talk glibly".
column6: Tā yòu zài shuǎshuài le.
column7: He is showing off again.
column9: To play with, to wield, to show off: 耍花招 "play tricks", 耍脾氣 "throw a tantrum", 耍帥 "show off, act cool", 耍寶 "clown around". It is a spoken word with a feel of playing with or putting on a performance. 耍嘴皮子 is "talk glibly".

column3: To swing, to throw off, to dump: 甩手 "swing one's arms", 甩掉 "shake off", 甩尾 "fishtail", 被甩了 "got dumped". It is spoken and strong: you get rid of something with a swing. The shape is built as the opposite of 用 "use".
column4: 他把头发一甩，转身走了。
column5: 他把頭髮一甩，轉身走了。
column6: Tā bǎ tóufa yī shuǎi, zhuǎnshēn zǒu le.
column7: He tossed his hair and turned and left.
column9: To swing, to throw off, to dump: 甩手 "swing one's arms", 甩掉 "shake off", 甩尾 "fishtail", 被甩了 "got dumped". It is spoken and strong: you get rid of something with a swing. The shape is built as the opposite of 用 "use".

column3: To decline, to fall off: 经济衰退 "recession", 记忆力衰退 "failing memory", 体力衰退, 视力衰退. It is for things getting weaker over time, health, economies, strength. 衰 "weak, decline" + 退 "retreat". Opposite of 成长 and 进步.
column6: Rén lǎo le, jìyìlì huì shuāituì.
column7: When people get old their memory declines.
column9: To decline, to fall off: 經濟衰退 "recession", 記憶力衰退 "failing memory", 體力衰退, 視力衰退. It is for things getting weaker over time, health, economies, strength. 衰 "weak, decline" + 退 "retreat". Opposite of 成長 and 進步.

column3: Twins: 双胞胎兄弟, 一对双胞胎, 龙凤胎 "boy and girl twins". 双 "pair" + 胞 "womb" + 胎 "fetus, birth". The three together name children born of the same womb at once. 胎 and 胞 both have 月 "flesh" on the left. Twins of the same sex that look alike are 同卵双胞胎 "identical twins".
column4: 他们是双胞胎，长得一模一样。
column5: 他們是雙胞胎，長得一模一樣。
column6: Tāmen shì shuāngbāotāi, zhǎng de yīmúyīyàng.
column7: They are twins and look exactly alike.
column9: Twins: 雙胞胎兄弟, 一對雙胞胎, 龍鳳胎 "boy and girl twins". 雙 "pair" + 胞 "womb" + 胎 "fetus, birth". The three together name children born of the same womb at once. 胎 and 胞 both have 月 "flesh" on the left. Twins of the same sex that look alike are 同卵雙胞胎 "identical twins".

column3: Negligence, to overlook: 一时疏忽 "a moment's carelessness", 因为疏忽 "due to carelessness", 疏忽了细节. Used both as a verb ("neglect") and as a noun ("an oversight"). The oversight is usually small and unintended. 疏 "sparse, thin" + 忽 "neglect". The last syllable is neutral.
column4: 因为一时疏忽，他忘了锁门。
column5: 因為一時疏忽，他忘了鎖門。
column6: Yīnwèi yīshí shūhu, tā wàng le suǒ mén.
column7: Through a moment of carelessness he forgot to lock the door.
column9: Negligence, to overlook: 一時疏忽 "a moment's carelessness", 因為疏忽 "due to carelessness", 疏忽了細節. Used both as a verb ("neglect") and as a noun ("an oversight"). The oversight is usually small and unintended. 疏 "sparse, thin" + 忽 "neglect". The last syllable is neutral.

column3: Tax: 税金 "tax payments", 缴税 "pay tax", 报税 "file a tax return", 营业税, 所得税 "income tax", 退税 "tax refund". 禾 "grain" on the left, since taxes were once paid in grain, and 兑 gives the sound (duì, shuì).
column6: Měi nián wǔyuè yào bàoshuì.
column7: You file your taxes in May every year.
column9: Tax: 稅金 "tax payments", 繳稅 "pay tax", 報稅 "file a tax return", 營業稅, 所得稅 "income tax", 退稅 "tax refund". 禾 "grain" on the left, since taxes were once paid in grain, and 兌 gives the sound (duì, shuì).

column3: Books as a whole, in a formal sense: 阅读书籍 "read books", 书籍出版, 各类书籍. It names books as a category, for libraries, publishers and notices, and has no classifier. In speech 书 is used. 书 "book" + 籍 "records, register", where 竹 "bamboo" at the top recalls old bamboo-strip books.
column6: Túshūguǎn lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng shūjí.
column7: The library has all kinds of books.
column9: Books as a whole, in a formal sense: 閱讀書籍 "read books", 書籍出版, 各類書籍. It names books as a category, for libraries, publishers and notices, and has no classifier. In speech 書 is used. 書 "book" + 籍 "records, register", where 竹 "bamboo" at the top recalls old bamboo-strip books.

column3: Smooth, along, favorable, and "to follow": 顺利 "smoothly", 顺路 "on the way", 顺便 "while one is at it", 孝顺 "obedient to parents", 顺着 "along". As a verb it means "to follow the direction of". 页 "head" is the meaning part and 川 "river" gives the sound.
column6: Nǐ shùn zhe zhè tiáo lù yīzhí zǒu.
column7: Just follow this road straight ahead.
column9: Smooth, along, favorable, and "to follow": 順利 "smoothly", 順路 "on the way", 順便 "while one is at it", 孝順 "obedient to parents", 順著 "along". As a verb it means "to follow the direction of". 頁 "head" is the meaning part and 川 "river" gives the sound.

column3: In passing, while one is at it, and "smooth, handy": 顺手关门 "close the door on the way", 顺手带走, and for tools: 这支笔很顺手 "this pen is handy". For things done as a side action without extra effort. 顺 "follow" + 手 "hand". 顺便 is similar, but 顺手 is about what the hand does.
column4: 你出门时顺手把垃圾带下去。
column5: 你出門時順手把垃圾帶下去。
column6: Nǐ chūmén shí shùnshǒu bǎ lājī dài xiàqù.
column7: Take the rubbish down with you as you go out.
column9: In passing, while one is at it, and "smooth, handy": 順手關門 "close the door on the way", 順手帶走, and for tools: 這支筆很順手 "this pen is handy". For things done as a side action without extra effort. 順 "follow" + 手 "hand". 順便 is similar, but 順手 is about what the hand does.

column3: Summer vacation period: 暑期打工 "summer job", 暑期班 "summer course", 暑期活动. It is the summer break of schools, usually July and August. 暑 "heat" + 期 "period". 暑假 is the general word for the summer vacation, and 暑期 is used for programs held in it.
column4: 他暑期在便利商店打工。
column5: 他暑期在便利商店打工。
column6: Tā shǔqī zài biànlì shāngdiàn dǎgōng.
column7: He works part time in a convenience store during the summer break.
column9: Summer vacation period: 暑期打工 "summer job", 暑期班 "summer course", 暑期活動. It is the summer break of schools, usually July and August. 暑 "heat" + 期 "period". 暑假 is the general word for the summer vacation, and 暑期 is used for programs held in it.

column3: Silk, thread, and "a trace, a thread-like strip": 丝绸 "silk", 蜘蛛丝 "spider silk", 肉丝 "shredded meat", 一丝希望 "a thread of hope". As a classifier it counts a trace of something: 一丝笑容.
column4: 我对未来还有一丝希望。
column5: 我對未來還有一絲希望。
column6: Wǒ duì wèilái hái yǒu yī sī xīwàng.
column7: I still have a thread of hope for the future.
column9: Silk, thread, and "a trace, a thread-like strip": 絲綢 "silk", 蜘蛛絲 "spider silk", 肉絲 "shredded meat", 一絲希望 "a thread of hope". As a classifier it counts a trace of something: 一絲笑容.

column3: To tear: 撕开 "tear open", 撕掉 "tear off", 撕破 "tear a hole in", 撕纸 "tear paper". You tear paper or cloth with your hands, and 扌 "hand" is the meaning part with 斯 giving the sound (sī, the same). It is for pulling something apart, and not for a rip caused by a sharp edge.
column6: Tā bǎ xìn sī chéng le liǎng bàn.
column7: He tore the letter in two.
column9: To tear: 撕開 "tear open", 撕掉 "tear off", 撕破 "tear a hole in", 撕紙 "tear paper". You tear paper or cloth with your hands, and 扌 "hand" is the meaning part with 斯 giving the sound (sī, the same). It is for pulling something apart, and not for a rip caused by a sharp edge.

column3: All over the place, everywhere: 四处走走 "walk around", 四处找 "look everywhere", 四处乱跑 "run around". 四 "four" + 处 "place", the four directions. It is spoken, and comes before a verb of movement or searching. The 处 here is read chù.
column4: 我四处找都找不到钥匙。
column5: 我四處找都找不到鑰匙。
column6: Wǒ sìchù zhǎo dōu zhǎo bu dào yàoshi.
column7: I looked everywhere and couldn't find the key.
column9: All over the place, everywhere: 四處走走 "walk around", 四處找 "look everywhere", 四處亂跑 "run around". 四 "four" + 處 "place", the four directions. It is spoken, and comes before a verb of movement or searching. The 處 here is read chù.

column3: Four-sided, and "everywhere, all directions": 四面八方 "from all directions", 来自四方, 四方形 "square". In writing it means all places: 游遍四方. 四 "four" + 方 "direction, side". 四方形 is a shape, a square.
column4: 游客从四方来到这座小城。
column5: 遊客從四方來到這座小城。
column6: Yóukè cóng sìfāng lái dào zhè zuò xiǎochéng.
column7: Visitors come to this small town from all around.
column9: Four-sided, and "everywhere, all directions": 四面八方 "from all directions", 來自四方, 四方形 "square". In writing it means all places: 遊遍四方. 四 "four" + 方 "direction, side". 四方形 is a shape, a square.

column3: The four seasons: 四季如春 "spring all year", 四季分明 "four distinct seasons", 一年四季. 四季如春 is said of mild places. 四 "four" + 季 "season". 季 is the word for a season, as in 春季 and 季节. It has a poetic tone.
column4: 这个地方四季都很舒服。
column5: 這個地方四季都很舒服。
column6: Zhège dìfang sìjì dōu hěn shūfu.
column7: The weather in this place is pleasant all year round.
column9: The four seasons: 四季如春 "spring all year", 四季分明 "four distinct seasons", 一年四季. 四季如春 is said of mild places. 四 "four" + 季 "season". 季 is the word for a season, as in 春季 and 季節. It has a poetic tone.

column3: Private for a school or hospital: 私立学校 "private school", 私立大学, 私立医院. 私 "private" + 立 "established". The opposite is 公立 "public". Pairs with 国立 and 市立.
column4: 她在一所私立学校教书。
column5: 她在一所私立學校教書。
column6: Tā zài yī suǒ sīlì xuéxiào jiāoshū.
column7: She teaches at a private school.
column9: Private for a school or hospital: 私立學校 "private school", 私立大學, 私立醫院. 私 "private" + 立 "established". The opposite is 公立 "public". Pairs with 國立 and 市立.

column3: To ponder, to think deeply: 思索问题 "think a problem over", 陷入思索 "sink into thought", 思索良久. It is a written word, for thinking that goes on for a while and ends with an answer. 思 "think" + 索 "search", with the idea of seeking an answer. 索 here is read suǒ.
column4: 他低着头，思索着这个问题。
column5: 他低著頭，思索著這個問題。
column6: Tā dī zhe tóu, sīsuǒ zhe zhège wèntí.
column7: He lowered his head, pondering the problem.
column9: To ponder, to think deeply: 思索問題 "think a problem over", 陷入思索 "sink into thought", 思索良久. It is a written word, for thinking that goes on for a while and ends with an answer. 思 "think" + 索 "search", with the idea of seeking an answer. 索 here is read suǒ.

column3: Death, to die: 死亡率 "death rate", 死亡人数 "number of dead", 死亡证明 "death certificate". It is a formal, news-style word for the event of death, not for grief or a person's own feelings. 死 "die" + 亡 "perish". In speech 死 or 去世 would be said.
column4: 这次事故造成三人死亡。
column5: 這次事故造成三人死亡。
column6: Zhè cì shìgù zàochéng sān rén sǐwáng.
column7: The accident caused three deaths.
column9: Death, to die: 死亡率 "death rate", 死亡人數 "number of dead", 死亡證明 "death certificate". It is a formal, news-style word for the event of death, not for grief or a person's own feelings. 死 "die" + 亡 "perish". In speech 死 or 去世 would be said.

column3: To raise, to rear animals: 饲养宠物 "keep pets", 饲养牛羊, 禁止饲养. It is the word for feeding and looking after animals, at a farm or at home. 饲 "feed" + 养 "nourish". 饲 has 饣 "food" at its left. A person's child is not 饲养 but 养.
column6: Wǒ jiā sìyǎng le yī zhī gǒu.
column7: My family keeps a dog.
column9: To raise, to rear animals: 飼養寵物 "keep pets", 飼養牛羊, 禁止飼養. It is the word for feeding and looking after animals, at a farm or at home. 飼 "feed" + 養 "nourish". 飼 has 飠 "food" at its left. A person's child is not 飼養 but 養.

column3: To see someone off: 去机场送行 "go to the airport to see someone off", 为他送行 "give him a send-off", 送行的人. You go along to the station or the airport as the traveler leaves. 送 "send" + 行 "travel". Here 行 is read xíng.
column4: 朋友们都到机场来送行。
column5: 朋友們都到機場來送行。
column6: Péngyoumen dōu dào jīchǎng lái sòngxíng.
column7: My friends all came to the airport to see me off.
column9: To see someone off: 去機場送行 "go to the airport to see someone off", 為他送行 "give him a send-off", 送行的人. You go along to the station or the airport as the traveler leaves. 送 "send" + 行 "travel". Here 行 is read xíng.

column3: Custom, common, vulgar: 风俗 "customs", 习俗 "traditions", 俗气 "tacky", 通俗 "popular, easy to understand", 世俗, 俗话. It is a bound form. 亻 "person" is the meaning part and 谷 gives a sound (gǔ, no longer close to sú). It has two sides: shared custom, and low or crude in taste.
column6: Guònián yǒu hěn duō chuántǒng xísú.
column7: There are many traditional customs at New Year.
column9: Custom, common, vulgar: 風俗 "customs", 習俗 "traditions", 俗氣 "tacky", 通俗 "popular, easy to understand", 世俗, 俗話. It is a bound form. 亻 "person" is the meaning part and 谷 gives a sound (gǔ, no longer close to sú). It has two sides: shared custom, and low or crude in taste.

column3: All told, when you think about it: 算起来 begins a statement drawn from counting or comparing: 算起来我们认识十年了 "all told we have known each other ten years", 算起来他是我的表哥 "by my reckoning he is my cousin". 算 "count" + 起来 "starting up", the count going from the beginning.
column4: 算起来，我们认识十年了。
column5: 算起來，我們認識十年了。
column6: Suànqǐlái, wǒmen rènshi shí nián le.
column7: All told, we have known each other for ten years.
column9: All told, when you think about it: 算起來 begins a statement drawn from counting or comparing: 算起來我們認識十年了 "all told we have known each other ten years", 算起來他是我的表哥 "by my reckoning he is my cousin". 算 "count" + 起來 "starting up", the count going from the beginning.

column3: Can be counted as, rather: 这算是好消息 "this counts as good news", 他算是我的老师. It labels something as belonging to a class, often with "more or less". It can also mean "at last": 今天算是做完了. 算 "count" + 是 "be".
column6: Zhè cì kǎoshì suànshì jiǎndān de.
column7: This exam counts as an easy one.
column9: Can be counted as, rather: 這算是好消息 "this counts as good news", 他算是我的老師. It labels something as belonging to a class, often with "more or less". It can also mean "at last": 今天算是做完了. 算 "count" + 是 "be".

column3: Common saying, proverb: 俗话说得好 "as the saying goes", 一句俗话. 俗 "common" + 话 "words". It is a saying that most people know and quote, such as 一分耕耘，一分收获. 俗话 is the set that people say, not literary quotations.
column6: Súhuà shuō: rén duō lìliàng dà.
column7: As the saying goes, many hands make light work.
column9: Common saying, proverb: 俗話說得好 "as the saying goes", 一句俗話. 俗 "common" + 話 "words". It is a saying that most people know and quote, such as 一分耕耘，一分收穫. 俗話 is the set that people say, not literary quotations.

column3: As the saying goes: 俗话说，... begins a proverb the speaker quotes to support a point. It is 俗话 plus 说 "say", and often 俗话说得好 "it's well said". People then give the proverb itself: 俗话说，一分耕耘，一分收获.
column4: 俗话说，早起的鸟儿有虫吃。
column5: 俗話說，早起的鳥兒有蟲吃。
column6: Súhuàshuō, zǎo qǐ de niǎor yǒu chóng chī.
column7: As the saying goes, the early bird catches the worm.
column9: As the saying goes: 俗話說，... begins a proverb the speaker quotes to support a point. It is 俗話 plus 說 "say", and often 俗話說得好 "it's well said". People then give the proverb itself: 俗話說，一分耕耘，一分收穫.

column3: Age, number of years: 多大岁数 "how old", 上了岁数 "getting on in years", 岁数大了 "old". It is spoken, mostly about older people: 老人家的岁数. 岁 "year of age" + 数 "number". The second syllable is neutral. To ask a child one asks 几岁.
column4: 爷爷的岁数大了，走路要小心。
column5: 爺爺的歲數大了，走路要小心。
column6: Yéye de suìshu dà le, zǒulù yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: Grandpa is getting on in years and must be careful when he walks.
column9: Age, number of years: 多大歲數 "how old", 上了歲數 "getting on in years", 歲數大了 "old". It is spoken, mostly about older people: 老人家的歲數. 歲 "year of age" + 數 "number". The second syllable is neutral. To ask a child one asks 幾歲.

column3: Plastic (Taiwan) and "synthetic resin": 塑胶袋 "plastic bag", 塑胶瓶, 塑胶玩具. In Taiwan 塑胶 is the word for plastic, and 塑料 is the mainland word. 塑 "mold, model" + 胶 "glue, gum". 胶 has 月 "flesh" on the left.
column6: Qǐng bù yào shǐyòng sùjiāo dài.
column7: Please do not use plastic bags.
column9: Plastic (Taiwan) and "synthetic resin": 塑膠袋 "plastic bag", 塑膠瓶, 塑膠玩具. In Taiwan 塑膠 is the word for plastic, and 塑料 is the mainland word. 塑 "mold, model" + 膠 "glue, gum". 膠 has 月 "flesh" on the left.

column3: To shrink, to draw back: 缩小 "make smaller", 缩短 "shorten", 缩水 "shrink in the wash", 缩写 "abbreviation", 退缩 "shrink back". It is a verb for things becoming shorter or smaller, or a person pulling back. 纟 "thread" is the meaning part, since thread pulls in.
column6: Yīfu xǐ le yǐhòu suō le.
column7: The clothes shrank after being washed.
column9: To shrink, to draw back: 縮小 "make smaller", 縮短 "shorten", 縮水 "shrink in the wash", 縮寫 "abbreviation", 退縮 "shrink back". It is a verb for things becoming shorter or smaller, or a person pulling back. 糹 "thread" is the meaning part, since thread pulls in.

column3: To shrink in the wash, and figuratively "to shrink, to be cut": 衣服缩水 "the clothes shrank", 预算缩水 "the budget shrank", 薪水缩水 "pay was cut". 缩 "shrink" + 水 "water". It is spoken.
column6: Zhè jiàn chènshān yī xǐ jiù suōshuǐ.
column7: This shirt shrinks as soon as it is washed.
column9: To shrink in the wash, and figuratively "to shrink, to be cut": 衣服縮水 "the clothes shrank", 預算縮水 "the budget shrank", 薪水縮水 "pay was cut". 縮 "shrink" + 水 "water". It is spoken.

column3: Vegetarian food, and "to eat vegetarian": 吃素食 "eat vegetarian", 素食餐厅, 素食者 "a vegetarian", 纯素 "vegan". A vegetarian can say 我吃素. 素 "plain" + 食 "food". 素 here means plain, without meat.
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng tígōng sùshí.
column7: This restaurant serves vegetarian food.
column9: Vegetarian food, and "to eat vegetarian": 吃素食 "eat vegetarian", 素食餐廳, 素食者 "a vegetarian", 純素 "vegan". A vegetarian can say 我吃素. 素 "plain" + 食 "food". 素 here means plain, without meat.

column3: To tread, to step on: 踏步 "march on the spot", 踏上 "step onto", 踏实 "down to earth", 脚踏车 "bicycle" (Taiwan's word), 踏青 "go for an outing in spring". 足 "foot" is the meaning part, and 沓 gives the sound (tà, the same). A foot comes down firmly on the thing.
column6: Tā tà shàng le xīn de lǚchéng.
column7: He set out on a new journey.
column9: To tread, to step on: 踏步 "march on the spot", 踏上 "step onto", 踏實 "down to earth", 腳踏車 "bicycle" (Taiwan's word), 踏青 "go for an outing in spring". 足 "foot" is the meaning part, and 沓 gives the sound (tà, the same). A foot comes down firmly on the thing.

column3: To collapse, to cave in: 房子塌了 "the house collapsed", 塌陷 "cave in", 塌方 "landslide". Also "to droop" and "to settle": 塌鼻子 "flat nose", 心里很塌实. 土 "earth" is the meaning part: things made of earth falling down. After an earthquake buildings may 倒塌.
column6: Dìzhèn hòu, nà dòng fángzi tā le.
column7: After the earthquake, that house collapsed.
column9: To collapse, to cave in: 房子塌了 "the house collapsed", 塌陷 "cave in", 塌方 "landslide". Also "to droop" and "to settle": 塌鼻子 "flat nose", 心裡很塌實. 土 "earth" is the meaning part: things made of earth falling down. After an earthquake buildings may 倒塌.

column3: Taiji, tai chi: 打太极拳 "practice tai chi", 练太极拳. A slow, flowing exercise; in parks many older people practice it in the early morning. 太极 "supreme ultimate" + 拳 "fist, boxing", so it is a martial art even when practiced for health. 拳 has 手 "hand" at the bottom.
column4: 公园里有很多人在打太极拳。
column5: 公園裡有很多人在打太極拳。
column6: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō rén zài dǎ tàijíquán.
column7: Many people are practicing tai chi in the park.
column9: Taiji, tai chi: 打太極拳 "practice tai chi", 練太極拳. A slow, flowing exercise; in parks many older people practice it in the early morning. 太極 "supreme ultimate" + 拳 "fist, boxing", so it is a martial art even when practiced for health. 拳 has 手 "hand" at the bottom.

column3: To explore, to feel for, and "to visit": 探路 "explore the way", 探险 "explore", 探望 "visit", 探病 "visit a sick person", 探头 "stick one's head out", 探索. As a verb it reaches forward to learn something. 扌 "hand" is the meaning part. Read tàn.
column6: Tā tàntóu kàn le kàn chuāngwài.
column7: He stuck his head out and looked outside.
column9: To explore, to feel for, and "to visit": 探路 "explore the way", 探險 "explore", 探望 "visit", 探病 "visit a sick person", 探頭 "stick one's head out", 探索. As a verb it reaches forward to learn something. 扌 "hand" is the meaning part. Read tàn.

column3: Classifier for trips: 去一趟 "make a trip", 跑一趟 "make a run", 来回两趟, 白跑一趟 "make the trip for nothing". It counts going somewhere and back, and also trains and buses on a run: 这一趟车. 走 "walk" is its meaning part, and 尚 the sound (shàng, only roughly like tàng).
column6: Wǒ zuótiān qù le yī tàng Táizhōng.
column7: Yesterday I made a trip to Taichung.
column9: Classifier for trips: 去一趟 "make a trip", 跑一趟 "make a run", 來回兩趟, 白跑一趟 "make the trip for nothing". It counts going somewhere and back, and also trains and buses on a run: 這一趟車. 走 "walk" is its meaning part, and 尚 the sound (shàng, only roughly like tàng).

column3: To scald, burn, "scalding hot", and "to perm, to iron": 烫伤 "a scald", 好烫 "very hot", 烫头发 "get a perm", 烫衣服 "iron clothes". It is for something hot enough to hurt the touch. 火 "fire" is the meaning part and 汤 "hot water" the sound (tāng, close to tàng).
column6: Xiǎoxīn, tāng hěn tàng!
column7: Careful, the soup is scalding hot!
column9: To scald, burn, "scalding hot", and "to perm, to iron": 燙傷 "a scald", 好燙 "very hot", 燙頭髮 "get a perm", 燙衣服 "iron clothes". It is for something hot enough to hurt the touch. 火 "fire" is the meaning part and 湯 "hot water" the sound (tāng, close to tàng).

column3: Tangyuan, glutinous rice balls: a dessert of balls of glutinous rice flour, filled or plain, in a sweet soup. Eaten at the Lantern Festival and, in Taiwan and southern China, at the winter solstice (冬至). 汤 "soup" + 圆 "round"; the round shape stands for family togetherness. 吃汤圆 means to eat them.
column6: Dōngzhì nà tiān wǒmen chī tāngyuán.
column7: On the winter solstice we eat tangyuan.
column9: Tangyuan, glutinous rice balls: a dessert of balls of glutinous rice flour, filled or plain, in a sweet soup. Eaten at the Lantern Festival and, in Taiwan and southern China, at the winter solstice (冬至). 湯 "soup" + 圓 "round"; the round shape stands for family togetherness. 吃湯圓 means to eat them.

column3: To visit one's relatives away from home, often a long trip: 回家探亲 "go home to see the family", 探亲假 "home leave". The visitor travels to where family lives. 探 "visit" + 亲 "relatives".
column6: Tā měi nián huíxiāng tànqīn yī cì.
column7: Once a year he goes back to his hometown to visit relatives.
column9: To visit one's relatives away from home, often a long trip: 回家探親 "go home to see the family", 探親假 "home leave". The visitor travels to where family lives. 探 "visit" + 親 "relatives".

column3: To investigate, to discuss in depth: 探讨问题 "look into a problem", 深入探讨 "discuss in depth", 探讨原因. It is a written word, for an issue studied and talked over with some seriousness: papers, meetings. 探 "probe" + 讨 "discuss". 讨 has 讠 "speech" on its left.
column4: 这个问题值得我们深入探讨。
column5: 這個問題值得我們深入探討。
column6: Zhège wèntí zhíde wǒmen shēnrù tàntǎo.
column7: This question deserves deeper discussion.
column9: To investigate, to discuss in depth: 探討問題 "look into a problem", 深入探討 "discuss in depth", 探討原因. It is a written word, for an issue studied and talked over with some seriousness: papers, meetings. 探 "probe" + 討 "discuss". 討 has 言 "speech" on its left.

column3: Stall, booth: 摆摊位 "set up a stall", 摊位费, 租摊位. At a market or a fair, the space a seller has. Night markets, 夜市, are full of them. 摊 "stall" + 位 "place, position". 摊子 is the stall itself, and 摊位 stresses the place it takes.
column4: 夜市里的摊位一个接一个。
column5: 夜市裡的攤位一個接一個。
column6: Yèshì lǐ de tānwèi yī ge jiē yī ge.
column7: The stalls at the night market go on one after another.
column9: Stall, booth: 擺攤位 "set up a stall", 攤位費, 租攤位. At a market or a fair, the space a seller has. Night markets, 夜市, are full of them. 攤 "stall" + 位 "place, position". 攤子 is the stall itself, and 攤位 stresses the place it takes.

column3: Blanket: 一条毯子, 盖毯子, 羊毛毯. A thick blanket for the bed or the sofa. 毯 "blanket, rug" + the neutral suffix 子. Rugs on the floor are 地毯. The second syllable is neutral.
column4: 天气冷，我盖了一条毯子。
column5: 天氣冷，我蓋了一條毯子。
column6: Tiānqì lěng, wǒ gài le yī tiáo tǎnzi.
column7: It was cold, so I covered myself with a blanket.
column9: Blanket: 一條毯子, 蓋毯子, 羊毛毯. A thick blanket for the bed or the sofa. 毯 "blanket, rug" + the neutral suffix 子. Rugs on the floor are 地毯. The second syllable is neutral.

column3: Stall, stand, and "a set-up, an operation": 摆摊子 "set up a stand", 小吃摊子 "snack stand", 烂摊子 "a mess" left to someone. The second sense is figurative: 摊子铺得太大 "has taken on too much". The 子 is neutral. 摊 has 扌 "hand" as the meaning part, the stall being set out by hand.
column4: 路边有一个卖水果的摊子。
column5: 路邊有一個賣水果的攤子。
column6: Lùbiān yǒu yī ge mài shuǐguǒ de tānzi.
column7: There is a fruit stall by the roadside.
column9: Stall, stand, and "a set-up, an operation": 擺攤子 "set up a stand", 小吃攤子 "snack stand", 爛攤子 "a mess" left to someone. The second sense is figurative: 攤子鋪得太大 "has taken on too much". The 子 is neutral. 攤 has 扌 "hand" as the meaning part, the stall being set out by hand.

column3: To ask for, to demand, "to invite": 讨钱 "ask for money", 讨饭 "beg", 讨价还价 "haggle", 讨厌 "dislike", 讨论 "discuss", 讨好 "curry favor", 讨债 "collect a debt". Mostly in compounds. 言 "speech" is the meaning part: you ask with words. 讨厌 "annoying" is the first one to know.
column6: Wǒ zuì tǎoyàn chī xiāngcài.
column7: I hate eating cilantro the most.
column9: To ask for, to demand, "to invite": 討錢 "ask for money", 討飯 "beg", 討價還價 "haggle", 討厭 "dislike", 討論 "discuss", 討好 "curry favor", 討債 "collect a debt". Mostly in compounds. 言 "speech" is the meaning part: you ask with words. 討厭 "annoying" is the first one to know.

column3: To take out, to fish out of a pocket or a hole: 掏出钱包 "take out a wallet", 掏口袋, 掏耳朵 "clean one's ears", 掏钱 "pay up". The hand goes in and comes out with something. 扌 "hand" is the meaning part, and 匋 gives the sound (táo, the same).
column6: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ tāo chū shǒujī.
column7: He pulled his phone out of his pocket.
column9: To take out, to fish out of a pocket or a hole: 掏出錢包 "take out a wallet", 掏口袋, 掏耳朵 "clean one's ears", 掏錢 "pay up". The hand goes in and comes out with something. 扌 "hand" is the meaning part, and 匋 gives the sound (táo, the same).

column3: To escape, to evade, to shirk: 逃避责任 "dodge responsibility", 逃避现实 "escape reality", 逃避问题. It is used for something unpleasant that you do not face, and often with a bad judgment. 逃 "flee" + 避 "avoid". Both characters have 辶 "walk".
column4: 不要逃避问题，要面对它。
column5: 不要逃避問題，要面對它。
column6: Bù yào táobì wèntí, yào miànduì tā.
column7: Don't run away from the problem, face it.
column9: To escape, to evade, to shirk: 逃避責任 "dodge responsibility", 逃避現實 "escape reality", 逃避問題. It is used for something unpleasant that you do not face, and often with a bad judgment. 逃 "flee" + 避 "avoid". Both characters have 辶 "walk".

column3: Ceramics, pottery and porcelain: 陶瓷杯 "ceramic cup", 陶瓷工艺, 陶瓷艺术. 陶 "pottery" + 瓷 "porcelain". 陶 has 阝 "mound" and 匋 "clay vessel" for the sound (táo, the same).
column4: 这个陶瓷杯是手工做的。
column5: 這個陶瓷杯是手工做的。
column6: Zhège táocí bēi shì shǒugōng zuò de.
column7: This ceramic cup was made by hand.
column9: Ceramics, pottery and porcelain: 陶瓷杯 "ceramic cup", 陶瓷工藝, 陶瓷藝術. 陶 "pottery" + 瓷 "porcelain". 陶 has 阝 "mound" and 匋 "clay vessel" for the sound (táo, the same).

column3: Naughty, mischievous: 淘气的孩子 "a naughty child", 他很淘气, 淘气鬼 "little rascal". For children, and the tone is fond: they play pranks and do not listen, but are not bad. 淘 "wash out" + 气 "temper".
column6: Zhège háizi hěn táoqì.
column7: This child is very naughty.
column9: Naughty, mischievous: 淘氣的孩子 "a naughty child", 他很淘氣, 淘氣鬼 "little rascal". For children, and the tone is fond: they play pranks and do not listen, but are not bad. 淘 "wash out" + 氣 "temper".

column3: Peach: 一颗桃子, 水蜜桃 "honey peach", 桃子很甜. 桃 "peach" + the neutral suffix 子. 桃 has 木 "tree" and 兆 for the sound (zhào, but now táo). Peaches are a symbol of long life in Chinese culture, and birthday buns for old people are shaped like them: 寿桃.
column6: Zhège táozi yòu dà yòu tián.
column7: This peach is big and sweet.
column9: Peach: 一顆桃子, 水蜜桃 "honey peach", 桃子很甜. 桃 "peach" + the neutral suffix 子. 桃 has 木 "tree" and 兆 for the sound (zhào, but now táo). Peaches are a symbol of long life in Chinese culture, and birthday buns for old people are shaped like them: 壽桃.

column3: Natural: 天然气 "natural gas", 天然资源 "natural resources", 天然食品, 天然的美. It means not made by humans: not processed, as found in nature. 天 "heaven, nature" + 然 "so". It is a popular word in ads for food, cloth and cosmetics.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn zhǐ mài tiānrán shípǐn.
column7: This shop sells only natural foods.
column9: Natural: 天然氣 "natural gas", 天然資源 "natural resources", 天然食品, 天然的美. It means not made by humans: not processed, as found in nature. 天 "heaven, nature" + 然 "so". It is a popular word in ads for food, cloth and cosmetics.

column3: Fields, open country: 田野风光 "the scenery of fields", 走在田野间, 田野调查 "field research". 田 "field" + 野 "wild, open land". It is a literary word for the countryside and open ground, and 田野调查 is the word of anthropologists.
column6: Wǒmen zài tiányě lǐ sànbù.
column7: We take a walk in the fields.
column9: Fields, open country: 田野風光 "the scenery of fields", 走在田野間, 田野調查 "field research". 田 "field" + 野 "wild, open land". It is a literary word for the countryside and open ground, and 田野調查 is the word of anthropologists.

column3: Catholicism, the Catholic Church: 天主教徒 "a Catholic", 天主教堂 "Catholic church", 信天主教. 天主 "Lord of Heaven" is the Chinese name for God in the Catholic tradition, and 教 means "teaching, religion". Protestant Christianity is 基督教.
column6: Tā jiā xìn Tiānzhǔjiào.
column7: Her family is Catholic.
column9: Catholicism, the Catholic Church: 天主教徒 "a Catholic", 天主教堂 "Catholic church", 信天主教. 天主 "Lord of Heaven" is the Chinese name for God in the Catholic tradition, and 教 means "teaching, religion". Protestant Christianity is 基督教.

column3: Treaty: 签订条约 "sign a treaty", 和平条约, 不平等条约 "unequal treaties". A written agreement between states, and a word of history and news. 条 "item, article" + 约 "agreement". 约 has 纟 "thread" on its left, as a tying agreement. 条 here is read tiáo.
column6: Liǎng guó qiāndìng le hépíng tiáoyuē.
column7: The two countries signed a peace treaty.
column9: Treaty: 簽訂條約 "sign a treaty", 和平條約, 不平等條約 "unequal treaties". A written agreement between states, and a word of history and news. 條 "item, article" + 約 "agreement". 約 has 糹 "thread" on its left, as a tying agreement. 條 here is read tiáo.

column3: Considerate, caring, intimate: 贴心的朋友 "a close friend", 贴心的服务 "thoughtful service", 真贴心 "how thoughtful". Taiwan uses this word a great deal for kindness that thinks ahead, from a friend or a shop. 贴 "stick close" + 心 "heart". It is a word of praise.
column4: 你想得真周到，太贴心了！
column5: 你想得真周到，太貼心了！
column6: Nǐ xiǎng de zhēn zhōudào, tài tiēxīn le!
column7: You thought of everything, that is so considerate!
column9: Considerate, caring, intimate: 貼心的朋友 "a close friend", 貼心的服務 "thoughtful service", 真貼心 "how thoughtful". Taiwan uses this word a great deal for kindness that thinks ahead, from a friend or a shop. 貼 "stick close" + 心 "heart". It is a word of praise.

column3: Body temperature: 量体温 "take someone's temperature", 体温计 "thermometer", 正常体温. A fever is 发烧. 体 "body" + 温 "temperature, warmth". 温 has 氵 "water" on its left.
column6: Nǐ de tǐwēn yǒudiǎn gāo.
column7: Your body temperature is a bit high.
column9: Body temperature: 量體溫 "take someone's temperature", 體溫計 "thermometer", 正常體溫. A fever is 發燒. 體 "body" + 溫 "temperature, warmth". 溫 has 氵 "water" on its left.

column3: To do earlier than planned, ahead of time: 提早出门 "leave early", 提早到达, 提早一个小时. It moves something to an earlier time than scheduled. 提 "lift, bring forward" + 早 "early". It can be a verb or an adverb. 提前 is much the same, in writing.
column4: 我们提早一个小时出发吧。
column5: 我們提早一個小時出發吧。
column6: Wǒmen tízǎo yī ge xiǎoshí chūfā ba.
column7: Let's set off an hour earlier.
column9: To do earlier than planned, ahead of time: 提早出門 "leave early", 提早到達, 提早一個小時. It moves something to an earlier time than scheduled. 提 "lift, bring forward" + 早 "early". It can be a verb or an adverb. 提前 is much the same, in writing.

column3: Copper: 铜板 "copper coin", 铜像 "bronze statue", 铜牌 "bronze medal", 铜管 "copper pipe". It covers copper and its alloys, so 铜像 is a bronze statue. 钅 "metal" is the meaning part and 同 gives the sound (tóng, the same).
column6: Guǎngchǎng shàng yǒu yī zuò tóngxiàng.
column7: There is a bronze statue in the square.
column9: Copper: 銅板 "copper coin", 銅像 "bronze statue", 銅牌 "bronze medal", 銅管 "copper pipe". It covers copper and its alloys, so 銅像 is a bronze statue. 釒 "metal" is the meaning part and 同 gives the sound (tóng, the same).

column3: Bucket, barrel, bin: 水桶 "water bucket", 垃圾桶 "trash can", 一桶水, 泡面桶. It is also a classifier: 一桶油 "a barrel of oil". 木 "wood" is the meaning part, since buckets were made of wood, and 甬 gives the sound (yǒng, close to tǒng).
column6: Qǐng bǎ lājī diū jìn lājītǒng.
column7: Please throw the rubbish in the trash can.
column9: Bucket, barrel, bin: 水桶 "water bucket", 垃圾桶 "trash can", 一桶水, 泡麵桶. It is also a classifier: 一桶油 "a barrel of oil". 木 "wood" is the meaning part, since buckets were made of wood, and 甬 gives the sound (yǒng, close to tǒng).

column3: Fellow countryman, compatriot, and "siblings of the same parents": 海外同胞 "countrymen abroad", 台湾同胞, 亲爱的同胞们 "dear fellow citizens", used in speeches. 同 "same" + 胞 "womb": born of the same womb, so the nation as one family. 胞 has 月 "flesh" on the left.
column4: 总统向全体同胞发表演说。
column5: 總統向全體同胞發表演說。
column6: Zǒngtǒng xiàng quántǐ tóngbāo fābiǎo yǎnshuō.
column7: The president gave a speech to all fellow citizens.
column9: Fellow countryman, compatriot, and "siblings of the same parents": 海外同胞 "countrymen abroad", 台灣同胞, 親愛的同胞們 "dear fellow citizens", used in speeches. 同 "same" + 胞 "womb": born of the same womb, so the nation as one family. 胞 has 月 "flesh" on the left.

column3: Communications, and "a news report": 通讯软体 "messaging app", 通讯录 "contacts list", 通讯设备, 通讯地址 "mailing address". Messaging apps are 通讯软体. 通 "through" + 讯 "news, message". 讯 has 讠 "speech" at the left.
column6: Wǒmen yòng tōngxùn ruǎntǐ liánluò.
column7: We keep in touch with a messaging app.
column9: Communications, and "a news report": 通訊軟體 "messaging app", 通訊錄 "contacts list", 通訊設備, 通訊地址 "mailing address". Messaging apps are 通訊軟體. 通 "through" + 訊 "news, message". 訊 has 言 "speech" at the left.

column3: Comrade, and today, especially in Taiwan, "gay person" or the LGBT community: 同志大游行 "the Pride parade", 同志婚姻. 同 "same" + 志 "aim, will": people with a common cause. In the older, political sense it is used for party members.
column4: 台北每年都有同志大游行。
column5: 台北每年都有同志大遊行。
column6: Táiběi měi nián dōu yǒu tóngzhì dà yóuxíng.
column7: Taipei has a Pride parade every year.
column9: Comrade, and today, especially in Taiwan, "gay person" or the LGBT community: 同志大遊行 "the Pride parade", 同志婚姻. 同 "same" + 志 "aim, will": people with a common cause. In the older, political sense it is used for party members.

column3: To rule, to govern a country or a people, often with the sense of one party in power: 统治者 "a ruler", 统治阶级 "the ruling class", 长期统治. 统 "unify" + 治 "govern". It is a word of history and politics, and tends to suggest power from above. For a government doing everyday work, 治理 or 管理 is used.
column4: 这个国家被一个政党统治了很多年。
column5: 這個國家被一個政黨統治了很多年。
column6: Zhège guójiā bèi yī ge zhèngdǎng tǒngzhì le hěn duō nián.
column7: This country was ruled by one party for many years.
column9: To rule, to govern a country or a people, often with the sense of one party in power: 統治者 "a ruler", 統治階級 "the ruling class", 長期統治. 統 "unify" + 治 "govern". It is a word of history and politics, and tends to suggest power from above. For a government doing everyday work, 治理 or 管理 is used.

column3: Through, by means of: 透过窗户 "through the window", 透过朋友认识 "get to know through a friend", 透过网路. It marks the way or the channel by which something happens. 透 "pass through" + 过 "go past". 通过 and 用 can often be used instead.
column4: 我是透过朋友认识他的。
column5: 我是透過朋友認識他的。
column6: Wǒ shì tòuguò péngyou rènshi tā de.
column7: I got to know him through a friend.
column9: Through, by means of: 透過窗戶 "through the window", 透過朋友認識 "get to know through a friend", 透過網路. It marks the way or the channel by which something happens. 透 "pass through" + 過 "go past". 通過 and 用 can often be used instead.

column3: To vote: 投票给他 "vote for him", 投票日, 投票所 "polling station", 投一票. A verb with its object inside, so one says 投了票 and 投了一票. 投 "cast" + 票 "ballot, ticket". 投票率 is the voting rate.
column4: 明天是投票日，你去投票了吗？
column5: 明天是投票日，你去投票了嗎？
column6: Míngtiān shì tóupiào rì, nǐ qù tóupiào le ma?
column7: Tomorrow is election day, have you voted?
column9: To vote: 投票給他 "vote for him", 投票日, 投票所 "polling station", 投一票. A verb with its object inside, so one says 投了票 and 投了一票. 投 "cast" + 票 "ballot, ticket". 投票率 is the voting rate.

column3: To surrender: 向敌人投降 "surrender to the enemy", 举手投降 "raise one's hands and surrender", 不投降. It is for war, for a contest, and in speech as a joke: 我投降 "I give up". 投 "throw in" + 降 "yield". Here 降 is read xiáng, not jiàng.
column6: Wǒ tóuxiáng, nǐ yíng le.
column7: I give up, you win.
column9: To surrender: 向敵人投降 "surrender to the enemy", 舉手投降 "raise one's hands and surrender", 不投降. It is for war, for a contest, and in speech as a joke: 我投降 "I give up". 投 "throw in" + 降 "yield". Here 降 is read xiáng, not jiàng.

column3: Bald: 秃头 "bald head", 秃子 "bald person", 秃了 "gone bald", 光秃秃 "bare, bald". It can also be said of a tree with no leaves or a hill with no trees. The old picture was 毛 "hair" over 儿 "person", worn into 禾 over 几.
column6: Dōngtiān de shù dōu tū le.
column7: The trees are all bare in winter.
column9: Bald: 禿頭 "bald head", 禿子 "bald person", 禿了 "gone bald", 光禿禿 "bare, bald". It can also be said of a tree with no leaves or a hill with no trees. The old picture was 毛 "hair" over a "person", worn into 禾 over a person.

column3: To overthrow, to overturn: 推翻政府 "overthrow a government", 推翻理论 "overturn a theory", 推翻原来的决定 "reverse a decision". 推 "push" + 翻 "turn over". It may be a ruler, a view, an earlier statement or a verdict that is turned over. 翻 has 羽 "feather" at the right.
column4: 新的证据推翻了原来的说法。
column5: 新的證據推翻了原來的說法。
column6: Xīn de zhèngjù tuīfān le yuánlái de shuōfǎ.
column7: The new evidence overturned the earlier account.
column9: To overthrow, to overturn: 推翻政府 "overthrow a government", 推翻理論 "overturn a theory", 推翻原來的決定 "reverse a decision". 推 "push" + 翻 "turn over". It may be a ruler, a view, an earlier statement or a verdict that is turned over. 翻 has 羽 "feather" at the right.

column3: To send back, to return: 退回商品 "return goods", 退回来 "be sent back", 被退回, and "to go back": 退回原位. It is used for an item rejected and returned by mail or in a shop. 退 "retreat" + 回 "back". A refund of money is 退款 or 退钱.
column6: Zhè jiàn shāngpǐn kěyǐ tuìhuí ma?
column7: Can this item be returned?
column9: To send back, to return: 退回商品 "return goods", 退回來 "be sent back", 被退回, and "to go back": 退回原位. It is used for an item rejected and returned by mail or in a shop. 退 "retreat" + 回 "back". A refund of money is 退款 or 退錢.

column3: Way, channel, means: 解决问题的途径 "a way to solve the problem", 合法途径 "legal means", 透过各种途径. It is a path for getting something done or learned. 途 "road" + 径 "path". Both have a walking part, 辶 and 彳. It is a formal word, and the thing is a means, not a literal path.
column4: 这是了解中国文化的好途径。
column5: 這是了解中國文化的好途徑。
column6: Zhè shì liǎojiě Zhōngguó wénhuà de hǎo tújìng.
column7: This is a good way to learn about Chinese culture.
column9: Way, channel, means: 解決問題的途徑 "a way to solve the problem", 合法途徑 "legal means", 透過各種途徑. It is a path for getting something done or learned. 途 "road" + 徑 "path". Both have a walking part, 辶 and 彳. It is a formal word, and the thing is a means, not a literal path.

column3: To swallow: 吞下去 "swallow", 吞药 "swallow a pill", 吞口水 "swallow saliva", 吞没 "embezzle". It is for swallowing whole, without chewing: 狼吞虎咽 is eating greedily. 口 "mouth" is the bottom part, and 天 gives the sound (tiān, close to tūn).
column6: Tā bǎ yào tūn xiàqù le.
column7: He swallowed the medicine.
column9: To swallow: 吞下去 "swallow", 吞藥 "swallow a pill", 吞口水 "swallow saliva", 吞沒 "embezzle". It is for swallowing whole, without chewing: 狼吞虎嚥 is eating greedily. 口 "mouth" is the bottom part, and 天 gives the sound (tiān, close to tūn).

column3: To drag, to tow, to mop: 拖地 "mop the floor", 拖车 "tow truck", 拖鞋 "slippers", 拖行李 "drag luggage". Also "to delay": 拖延 "procrastinate", 拖时间 "stall for time". 扌 "hand" is the meaning part. 拖鞋 are the flip-flops and house slippers one wears at home.
column6: Wǒ zhōumò yào zài jiā tuō dì.
column7: I will mop the floor at home this weekend.
column9: To drag, to tow, to mop: 拖地 "mop the floor", 拖車 "tow truck", 拖鞋 "slippers", 拖行李 "drag luggage". Also "to delay": 拖延 "procrastinate", 拖時間 "stall for time". 扌 "hand" is the meaning part. 拖鞋 are the flip-flops and house slippers one wears at home.

column3: Appropriate, proper, well done: 处理得很妥当 "handled properly", 安排妥当 "all arranged", 不太妥当 "not quite proper". It speaks of a way of handling something that leaves no problem. 妥 "settled" + 当 "suitable". The 当 is read dàng, and in the list it is neutral.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì chǔlǐ de hěn tuǒdang.
column7: This matter was handled very properly.
column9: Appropriate, proper, well done: 處理得很妥當 "handled properly", 安排妥當 "all arranged", 不太妥當 "not quite proper". It speaks of a way of handling something that leaves no problem. 妥 "settled" + 當 "suitable". The 當 is read dàng, and in the list it is neutral.

column3: Nursery, day-care center: 托儿所 "nursery", 送孩子去托儿所, 托儿所老师. For small children before kindergarten. 托 "entrust" + 儿 "child" + 所 "place". The 儿 here is a full syllable, ér, not an ending.
column4: 妈妈每天送弟弟去托儿所。
column5: 媽媽每天送弟弟去托兒所。
column6: Māma měitiān sòng dìdi qù tuō'érsuǒ.
column7: Mom takes my little brother to nursery every day.
column9: Nursery, day-care center: 托兒所 "nursery", 送孩子去托兒所, 托兒所老師. For small children before kindergarten. 托 "entrust" + 兒 "child" + 所 "place". The 兒 here is a full syllable, ér, not an ending.

column3: Properly, satisfactorily: 妥善处理 "handle properly", 妥善保管 "store carefully", 妥善安排. It describes an action done fully and with care so that nothing goes wrong, and it is mainly an adverb before a verb. 妥 "settled" + 善 "good". 妥 shows a hand 爫 over a woman 女, in the sense of calming.
column6: Qǐng tuǒshàn bǎoguǎn nǐ de zhèngjiàn.
column7: Please keep your documents safe.
column9: Properly, satisfactorily: 妥善處理 "handle properly", 妥善保管 "store carefully", 妥善安排. It describes an action done fully and with care so that nothing goes wrong, and it is mainly an adverb before a verb. 妥 "settled" + 善 "good". 妥 shows a hand 爫 over a woman 女, in the sense of calming.

column3: To compromise: 做出妥协 "make a compromise", 不肯妥协 "refuse to compromise", 双方妥协. Each side gives up something to reach an agreement. 妥 "settled" + 协 "cooperate". It may sound like giving in, so it can be critical: 不要向压力妥协.
column4: 双方最后各让一步，达成妥协。
column5: 雙方最後各讓一步，達成妥協。
column6: Shuāngfāng zuìhòu gè ràng yī bù, dáchéng tuǒxié.
column7: In the end both sides gave way a little and reached a compromise.
column9: To compromise: 做出妥協 "make a compromise", 不肯妥協 "refuse to compromise", 雙方妥協. Each side gives up something to reach an agreement. 妥 "settled" + 協 "cooperate". It may sound like giving in, so it can be critical: 不要向壓力妥協.

column3: Books in a library or shop: 图书馆 "library", 图书证 "library card", 儿童图书. It is a word for books as a collection, and a modifier. 图 "picture, chart" + 书 "book". The library is 图书馆 and a bookstore is 书店.
column4: 学校图书馆有很多图书。
column5: 學校圖書館有很多圖書。
column6: Xuéxiào túshūguǎn yǒu hěn duō túshū.
column7: The school library has many books.
column9: Books in a library or shop: 圖書館 "library", 圖書證 "library card", 兒童圖書. It is a word for books as a collection, and a modifier. 圖 "picture, chart" + 書 "book". The library is 圖書館 and a bookstore is 書店.

column3: A small seal or stamp, used in Taiwan in place of a signature on many documents, such as at the bank or the post office: 盖图章 "to stamp with one's seal". 图 "picture, plan" + 章 "seal"; 章 also means "chapter". 印章 is the more general word.
column6: Zhè fèn wénjiàn xūyào gài túzhāng.
column7: This document needs to be stamped with a seal.
column9: A small seal or stamp, used in Taiwan in place of a signature on many documents, such as at the bank or the post office: 蓋圖章 "to stamp with one's seal". 圖 "picture, plan" + 章 "seal"; 章 also means "chapter". 印章 is the more general word.

column3: To dig a hole or to scoop something out: 挖洞, 挖土, 挖井 "dig a well". It takes the thing dug as its object. The hand 扌 on the left shows the action, and the right part 穵 is the hollow that is dug out and also gives the sound.
column4: 他在院子里挖了一个洞。
column5: 他在院子裡挖了一個洞。
column6: Tā zài yuànzi lǐ wā le yī ge dòng.
column7: He dug a hole in the yard.
column9: To dig a hole or to scoop something out: 挖洞, 挖土, 挖井 "dig a well". It takes the thing dug as its object. The hand 扌 on the left shows the action, and the right part 穵 is the hollow that is dug out and also gives the sound.

column3: Crooked, slanting, not straight: 挂歪了 "hung crooked", 歪着头 "with the head tilted". Also "devious" for ideas and ways: 歪主意 "a bad idea". The character is simply 不 "not" over 正 "straight", so it is the opposite of 正.
column6: Zhè zhāng huà guà wāi le.
column7: This picture is hanging crooked.
column9: Crooked, slanting, not straight: 掛歪了 "hung crooked", 歪著頭 "with the head tilted". Also "devious" for ideas and ways: 歪主意 "a bad idea". The character is simply 不 "not" over 正 "straight", so it is the opposite of 正.

column3: The outward look of a person or thing, what you see before you know it: 外表很漂亮 "looks very nice". It often sets the surface against what is inside: 不要只看外表 "do not judge by appearances". 外 "outside" + 表 "surface". 外观 is close but is used more for objects and buildings.
column6: Bù yào zhǐ kàn wàibiǎo.
column7: Do not judge only by appearances.
column9: The outward look of a person or thing, what you see before you know it: 外表很漂亮 "looks very nice". It often sets the surface against what is inside: 不要只看外表 "do not judge by appearances". 外 "outside" + 表 "surface". 外觀 is close but is used more for objects and buildings.

column3: The outside of something, or "external": 大楼的外部 "the outside of the building", 外部因素 "external factors". Its opposite is 内部. It is more written and technical than 外面, which is the everyday word for "outside" as a place.
column4: 这栋大楼的外部需要整修。
column5: 這棟大樓的外部需要整修。
column6: Zhè dòng dàlóu de wàibù xūyào zhěngxiū.
column7: The outside of this building needs repairs.
column9: The outside of something, or "external": 大樓的外部 "the outside of the building", 外部因素 "external factors". Its opposite is 內部. It is more written and technical than 外面, which is the everyday word for "outside" as a place.

column3: To go out, to leave home or the office for some purpose: 他外出了 "he is out", 外出旅行 "go away on a trip". It sounds a little formal and is typical on notices: 外出用餐, 外出办事. For a plain "go out" in speech, say 出去.
column4: 他今天外出了，不在办公室。
column5: 他今天外出了，不在辦公室。
column6: Tā jīntiān wàichū le, bù zài bàngōngshì.
column7: He is out today and is not in the office.
column9: To go out, to leave home or the office for some purpose: 他外出了 "he is out", 外出旅行 "go away on a trip". It sounds a little formal and is typical on notices: 外出用餐, 外出辦事. For a plain "go out" in speech, say 出去.

column3: The outward appearance of a building, a product or a person: 外观设计 "the exterior design", 外观很新 "looks new". It is about the shape and look of the thing as a whole. 观 has 见 "see" for the meaning, and the same 观 turns up in 观光 "sightseeing" and 观点 "point of view".
column6: Zhè liàng chē de wàiguān hěn shímáo.
column7: The look of this car is very stylish.
column9: The outward appearance of a building, a product or a person: 外觀設計 "the exterior design", 外觀很新 "looks new". It is about the shape and look of the thing as a whole. 觀 has 見 "see" for the meaning, and the same 觀 turns up in 觀光 "sightseeing" and 觀點 "point of view".

column3: A layman, an amateur: 我对电脑是外行 "I am a layman with computers". It means someone who is outside a trade and does not know its ways. The opposite is 内行 "an expert, one of the trade". 行 here is read háng, "line of work", not xíng.
column6: Wǒ duì diànnǎo shì wàiháng.
column7: I am a layman when it comes to computers.
column9: A layman, an amateur: 我對電腦是外行 "I am a layman with computers". It means someone who is outside a trade and does not know its ways. The opposite is 內行 "an expert, one of the trade". 行 here is read háng, "line of work", not xíng.

column3: Surgery, as a branch of hospital medicine: 外科医生 "surgeon", 外科手术 "a surgical operation". At a hospital it is the department you go to for injuries and operations, as against 内科 "internal medicine". 科 is "branch, department" and also turns up in 科学 and 科目.
column6: Tā shì yīyuàn de wàikē yīshēng.
column7: He is a surgeon at the hospital.
column9: Surgery, as a branch of hospital medicine: 外科醫生 "surgeon", 外科手術 "a surgical operation". At a hospital it is the department you go to for injuries and operations, as against 內科 "internal medicine". 科 is "branch, department" and also turns up in 科學 and 科目.

column3: Those of a younger generation than you in the family or in a trade, the opposite of 长辈: 对晚辈要亲切 "be kind to those younger than you". The speaker also uses it humbly of himself in front of an elder, 晚辈 "your junior". 晚 means "late", so the word is those who came late. 辈 is "generation" and shows up in 前辈 "senior, predecessor".
column6: Tā duì wǎnbèi zǒngshì hěn qīnqiè.
column7: He is always kind to the younger ones.
column9: Those of a younger generation than you in the family or in a trade, the opposite of 長輩: 對晚輩要親切 "be kind to those younger than you". The speaker also uses it humbly of himself in front of an elder, 晚輩 "your junior". 晚 means "late", so the word is those who came late. 輩 is "generation" and shows up in 前輩 "senior, predecessor".

column3: To be finished or completed, said of preparations, procedures or a performance: 准备完毕 "preparations are complete", 检查完毕. It is a formal word for a thing that is wholly done, often at the end of a sentence in announcements. In speech 好了 or 完了 are used.
column6: Zhǔnbèi wánbì, kěyǐ chūfā le.
column7: Preparations are complete and we can set off.
column9: To be finished or completed, said of preparations, procedures or a performance: 準備完畢 "preparations are complete", 檢查完畢. It is a formal word for a thing that is wholly done, often at the end of a sentence in announcements. In speech 好了 or 完了 are used.

column3: To look into the distance, to look toward: 望着远方 "gaze into the distance", 望向窗外. It is more literary than 看. It also means "to hope" in 希望, 渴望 and 失望. In the character, a person standing 王 looks up at the moon 月.
column4: 他望着远方，一句话也没说。
column5: 他望著遠方，一句話也沒說。
column6: Tā wàng zhe yuǎnfāng, yī jù huà yě méi shuō.
column7: He gazed into the distance and said not a word.
column9: To look into the distance, to look toward: 望著遠方 "gaze into the distance", 望向窗外. It is more literary than 看. It also means "to hope" in 希望, 渴望 and 失望. In the character, a person standing 王 looks up at the moon 月.

column3: A joke, or to joke: 开玩笑 "to make a joke, to tease", 别开玩笑了 "stop joking", 这不是玩笑 "this is no joke". 玩 "play" + 笑 "laugh". 开玩笑 is the form you hear most, and 你开玩笑吧 means "you must be kidding".
column6: Nǐ bié kāi wánxiào le!
column7: Stop joking!
column9: A joke, or to joke: 開玩笑 "to make a joke, to tease", 別開玩笑了 "stop joking", 這不是玩笑 "this is no joke". 玩 "play" + 笑 "laugh". 開玩笑 is the form you hear most, and 你開玩笑吧 means "you must be kidding".

column3: To bend at the waist, to stoop: 弯腰捡东西 "bend down to pick something up", 弯腰鞠躬 "bow". 弯 "bend" has 弓 "bow" below, the bent shape, and 腰 "waist" has the flesh part ⺼ on the left, as other body parts do (腿, 脸).
column6: Tā wānyāo jiǎn qǐ le bǐ.
column7: He bent down and picked up the pen.
column9: To bend at the waist, to stoop: 彎腰撿東西 "bend down to pick something up", 彎腰鞠躬 "bow". 彎 "bend" has 弓 "bow" below, the bent shape, and 腰 "waist" has the flesh part ⺼ on the left, as other body parts do (腿, 臉).

column3: The word used in Taiwan for cooking gas and the gas supply: 瓦斯炉 "gas stove", 瓦斯桶 "gas cylinder", 瓦斯费 "gas bill", 瓦斯漏气 "a gas leak". It is a loanword for "gas": the characters are chosen for sound, and 瓦 here has nothing to do with roof tiles. The mainland says 煤气 or 天然气.
column6: Zhǔ wán fàn jìde guān wǎsī.
column7: After cooking, remember to turn off the gas.
column9: The word used in Taiwan for cooking gas and the gas supply: 瓦斯爐 "gas stove", 瓦斯桶 "gas cylinder", 瓦斯費 "gas bill", 瓦斯漏氣 "a gas leak". It is a loanword for "gas": the characters are chosen for sound, and 瓦 here has nothing to do with roof tiles. The mainland says 煤氣 or 天然氣.

column3: Not yet or "not", a written negative: 未来 "future", 未婚 "unmarried", 尚未 "not yet", 未必 "not necessarily". Before a verb it means "has not": 未回信 "has not replied". It is at home in formal writing, notices and set words; in speech people say 还没 or 没有.
column6: Tā dào xiànzài hái wèi huíxìn.
column7: He has not replied even now.
column9: Not yet or "not", a written negative: 未來 "future", 未婚 "unmarried", 尚未 "not yet", 未必 "not necessarily". Before a verb it means "has not": 未回信 "has not replied". It is at home in formal writing, notices and set words; in speech people say 還沒 or 沒有.

column3: A tail, or the end of something: 尾巴 is the common word for an animal's tail. Alone, 尾 is the classifier for fish: 一尾鱼 "one fish", 两尾虾; it is also in 结尾 "ending" and 年尾 "end of the year". The character shows a tail 毛 "hair" trailing from a body 尸.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng wěi yú.
column7: I bought two fish.
column9: A tail, or the end of something: 尾巴 is the common word for an animal's tail. Alone, 尾 is the classifier for fish: 一尾魚 "one fish", 兩尾蝦; it is also in 結尾 "ending" and 年尾 "end of the year". The character shows a tail 毛 "hair" trailing from a body 尸.

column3: Why, the written form of 为什么: 为何如此 "why is it so", 为何不 "why not". It stands before the verb and is used in writing and speeches, and in questions that sound serious or literary. 何 is the old question word "what" and also appears in 如何 "how" and 任何 "any".
column6: Nǐ wèihé bù zǎodiǎn gàosù wǒ?
column7: Why did you not tell me sooner?
column9: Why, the written form of 為什麼: 為何如此 "why is it so", 為何不 "why not". It stands before the verb and is used in writing and speeches, and in questions that sound serious or literary. 何 is the old question word "what" and also appears in 如何 "how" and 任何 "any".

column3: Unmarried, as a status on forms or in description: 未婚 as against 已婚 "married". It is 未 "not yet" + 婚 "marry", so it means "not yet married" and not "will never marry". Forms ask 未婚 or 已婚. In speech, 单身 "single" is more common for someone not in a relationship.
column6: Tā hái wèihūn, yī ge rén zhù.
column7: She is still unmarried and lives alone.
column9: Unmarried, as a status on forms or in description: 未婚 as against 已婚 "married". It is 未 "not yet" + 婚 "marry", so it means "not yet married" and not "will never marry". Forms ask 未婚 or 已婚. In speech, 單身 "single" is more common for someone not in a relationship.

column3: A crisis: 经济危机 "an economic crisis", 面临危机 "to face a crisis", 危机处理 "crisis management". 危 means "danger" (a person on the edge of a cliff, from the character's shape) and 机 here is "turning point, critical moment", as in 机会 and 转机.
column6: Gōngsī zhèng miànlín yī chǎng wēijī.
column7: The company is facing a crisis.
column9: A crisis: 經濟危機 "an economic crisis", 面臨危機 "to face a crisis", 危機處理 "crisis management". 危 means "danger" (a person on the edge of a cliff, from the character's shape) and 機 here is "turning point, critical moment", as in 機會 and 轉機.

column3: MSG, the white seasoning powder: 加味精 "add MSG". 味 "taste" + 精 "essence". A restaurant may advertise 不加味精 "no MSG added". 精 means "refined, pure" and has 米 "rice" on its left, as in 精米 and 精华.
column4: 做菜时不一定要放味精。
column5: 做菜時不一定要放味精。
column6: Zuò cài shí bù yīdìng yào fàng wèijīng.
column7: You do not always have to add MSG when cooking.
column9: MSG, the white seasoning powder: 加味精 "add MSG". 味 "taste" + 精 "essence". A restaurant may advertise 不加味精 "no MSG added". 精 means "refined, pure" and has 米 "rice" on its left, as in 精米 and 精華.

column3: To feel wronged and hurt because you were treated unfairly, or the feeling itself: 觉得很委屈, 受委屈 "to be wronged", 别委屈自己 "do not make things hard on yourself". It can also mean to make someone put up with less: 委屈你了 "sorry to put you through this". The second syllable is neutral: wěiqu.
column4: 他觉得很委屈，一句话也不想说。
column5: 他覺得很委屈，一句話也不想說。
column6: Tā juéde hěn wěiqu, yī jù huà yě bù xiǎng shuō.
column7: He felt wronged and did not want to say a word.
column9: To feel wronged and hurt because you were treated unfairly, or the feeling itself: 覺得很委屈, 受委屈 "to be wronged", 別委屈自己 "do not make things hard on yourself". It can also mean to make someone put up with less: 委屈你了 "sorry to put you through this". The second syllable is neutral: wěiqu.

column3: Vitamins: 维生素C "vitamin C", 补充维生素 "take vitamins". 维 "maintain" + 生 "life" + 素 "element", so the word is "elements that keep life going". It is the formal and written name, often found in articles and on packaging; in speech 维他命 is common in Taiwan.
column4: 多吃水果可以补充维生素。
column5: 多吃水果可以補充維生素。
column6: Duō chī shuǐguǒ kěyǐ bǔchōng wéishēngsù.
column7: Eating more fruit can top up your vitamins.
column9: Vitamins: 維生素C "vitamin C", 補充維生素 "take vitamins". 維 "maintain" + 生 "life" + 素 "element", so the word is "elements that keep life going". It is the formal and written name, often found in articles and on packaging; in speech 維他命 is common in Taiwan.

column3: Vitamin, the spoken form, a loanword from "vitamin": 吃维他命 "take vitamins", 维他命C. The characters were picked for sound. 他 and 命 give "he" and "life" and carry no meaning here. It is the spoken word; 维生素 is for articles and labels.
column6: Wǒ měitiān chī yī kē wéitāmìng.
column7: I take one vitamin every day.
column9: Vitamin, the spoken form, a loanword from "vitamin": 吃維他命 "take vitamins", 維他命C. The characters were picked for sound. 他 and 命 give "he" and "life" and carry no meaning here. It is the spoken word; 維生素 is for articles and labels.

column3: To threaten, to put under threat: 威胁别人 "threaten others", 受到威胁 "to be threatened". The thing threatened can be a person or a safety: 威胁健康 "a threat to health". It is also used as a noun, 一种威胁. 胁 is the flank of the body.
column4: 他威胁要把这件事说出去。
column5: 他威脅要把這件事說出去。
column6: Tā wēixié yào bǎ zhè jiàn shì shuō chūqù.
column7: He threatened to tell everyone about this.
column9: To threaten, to put under threat: 威脅別人 "threaten others", 受到威脅 "to be threatened". The thing threatened can be a person or a safety: 威脅健康 "a threat to health". It is also used as a noun, 一種威脅. 脅 is the flank of the body.

column3: A member of a committee: 委员 sits on a 委员会, as in 立法委员 "legislator" in Taiwan, 校务委员 and 评审委员. It names the person, and 委员会 the body. 委 has the meaning "entrust", and 员 "member" is the same as in 人员 and 会员.
column4: 这位委员提出了不同的意见。
column5: 這位委員提出了不同的意見。
column6: Zhè wèi wěiyuán tíchū le bù tóng de yìjiàn.
column7: This committee member raised a different opinion.
column9: A member of a committee: 委員 sits on a 委員會, as in 立法委員 "legislator" in Taiwan, 校務委員 and 評審委員. It names the person, and 委員會 the body. 委 has the meaning "entrust", and 員 "member" is the same as in 人員 and 會員.

column3: A kiss, or to kiss: 吻了她一下 "kissed her", 一个吻 "a kiss", 飞吻 "blow a kiss". The mouth 口 on the left shows the part used, and 勿 on the right gives the sound (it still sounds alike: wěn and wù).
column4: 他在她的脸上吻了一下。
column5: 他在她的臉上吻了一下。
column6: Tā zài tā de liǎn shàng wěn le yīxià.
column7: He gave her a kiss on the cheek.
column9: A kiss, or to kiss: 吻了她一下 "kissed her", 一個吻 "a kiss", 飛吻 "blow a kiss". The mouth 口 on the left shows the part used, and 勿 on the right gives the sound (it still sounds alike: wěn and wù).

column3: To warm something up, to heat it gently: 把牛奶温一下 "warm the milk a little", 温酒. As an adjective it means "warm", not hot: 温水. It also forms 气温, 体温, 温度 and 温柔 "gentle". The 氵 "water" on the left fits warm water.
column6: Bǎ niúnǎi wēn yīxià zài hē.
column7: Warm the milk up a little before drinking it.
column9: To warm something up, to heat it gently: 把牛奶溫一下 "warm the milk a little", 溫酒. As an adjective it means "warm", not hot: 溫水. It also forms 氣溫, 體溫, 溫度 and 溫柔 "gentle". The 氵 "water" on the left fits warm water.

column3: Stationery: 文具店 "stationery shop", 文具用品 "stationery supplies". It covers pens, erasers, rulers and other things used for writing and for school. 文 "writing" + 具 "tool", so it is the tools of writing. 具 shows up in 工具 "tool" and 家具 "furniture".
column4: 开学前，我们去文具店买笔和本子。
column5: 開學前，我們去文具店買筆和本子。
column6: Kāixué qián, wǒmen qù wénjù diàn mǎi bǐ hé běnzi.
column7: Before school starts, we go to the stationery shop to buy pens and notebooks.
column9: Stationery: 文具店 "stationery shop", 文具用品 "stationery supplies". It covers pens, erasers, rulers and other things used for writing and for school. 文 "writing" + 具 "tool", so it is the tools of writing. 具 shows up in 工具 "tool" and 家具 "furniture".

column3: A diploma, a certificate of graduation: 大学文凭 "university diploma", 拿到文凭 "get a diploma". 文 "writing" + 凭 "proof, evidence". It carries the idea that the paper proves something to employers, which is why articles often talk about 文凭不等于能力 "a diploma is not the same as ability".
column4: 有了文凭，比较容易找工作。
column5: 有了文憑，比較容易找工作。
column6: Yǒu le wénpíng, bǐjiào róngyì zhǎo gōngzuò.
column7: With a diploma, it is easier to find work.
column9: A diploma, a certificate of graduation: 大學文憑 "university diploma", 拿到文憑 "get a diploma". 文 "writing" + 憑 "proof, evidence". It carries the idea that the paper proves something to employers, which is why articles often talk about 文憑不等於能力 "a diploma is not the same as ability".

column3: Cultural relics, objects from the past that are kept for their history: 出土文物 "excavated relics", 故宫文物 "the Palace Museum's treasures", 保护文物 "protect relics". 文 "culture" + 物 "thing". 物 has 牛 "ox" on the left and 勿 on the right for the sound.
column4: 博物馆里有很多古代文物。
column5: 博物館裡有很多古代文物。
column6: Bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu hěn duō gǔdài wénwù.
column7: There are many ancient relics in the museum.
column9: Cultural relics, objects from the past that are kept for their history: 出土文物 "excavated relics", 故宮文物 "the Palace Museum's treasures", 保護文物 "protect relics". 文 "culture" + 物 "thing". 物 has 牛 "ox" on the left and 勿 on the right for the sound.

column3: Do not, a written prohibition: 请勿吸烟 "no smoking", 请勿打扰 "please do not disturb", 请勿停车. It appears on signs and notices and is never used in a conversation, where you say 不要 or 别. It goes before the verb. The character began as a knife with blood or flecks falling from it.
column6: Qǐng wù xīyān.
column7: No smoking, please.
column9: Do not, a written prohibition: 請勿吸菸 "no smoking", 請勿打擾 "please do not disturb", 請勿停車. It appears on signs and notices and is never used in a conversation, where you say 不要 or 別. It goes before the verb. The character began as a knife with blood or flecks falling from it.

column3: A mistake, or to miss, harm or delay, and "by mistake" before a verb: 误把盐当成糖 "took salt for sugar". It is mostly met in compounds: 错误, 误会 "misunderstanding", 耽误 "to delay", 误点 "late (of trains)". 讠 "speech" is the meaning part and 吴 the sound.
column6: Tā wù bǎ yán dàngchéng le táng.
column7: He mistook the salt for sugar.
column9: A mistake, or to miss, harm or delay, and "by mistake" before a verb: 誤把鹽當成糖 "took salt for sugar". It is mostly met in compounds: 錯誤, 誤會 "misunderstanding", 耽誤 "to delay", 誤點 "late (of trains)". 言 "speech" is the meaning part and 吳 the sound.

column3: Fog or mist: 起雾 "fog comes up", 大雾 "heavy fog", 浓雾. 雾 has 雨 "rain" at the top for the weather and 务 below for the sound (wù, the same). Another weather word with this top is 雪 and 雷.
column4: 今天早上有大雾，路上要小心。
column5: 今天早上有大霧，路上要小心。
column6: Jīntiān zǎoshang yǒu dà wù, lùshàng yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: There is heavy fog this morning, so be careful on the road.
column9: Fog or mist: 起霧 "fog comes up", 大霧 "heavy fog", 濃霧. 霧 has 雨 "rain" at the top for the weather and 務 below for the sound (wù, the same). Another weather word with this top is 雪 and 雷.

column3: Dance as an art, or dancing: 学舞蹈 "learn dance", 民族舞蹈 "folk dance", 舞蹈教室 "dance studio". It is the word for the art form or a school subject. For the act of dancing, 跳舞 is the verb. 舞 and 蹈 both mean dance; 蹈 has 足 "foot" for meaning, and 舞 has feet 舛 at its bottom.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xué wǔdǎo.
column7: She has studied dance since she was small.
column9: Dance as an art, or dancing: 學舞蹈 "learn dance", 民族舞蹈 "folk dance", 舞蹈教室 "dance studio". It is the word for the art form or a school subject. For the act of dancing, 跳舞 is the verb. 舞 and 蹈 both mean dance; 蹈 has 足 "foot" for meaning, and 舞 has feet 舛 at its bottom.

column3: To be late, said of trains, flights and buses: 火车误点了 "the train is late", 班机误点. It is the exact word for public transport running behind time. The reverse is 准点 "on time". 误 "miss, delay" + 点 "point of time". Not used for people being late: that is 迟到.
column6: Huǒchē yòu wùdiǎn le.
column7: The train is late again.
column9: To be late, said of trains, flights and buses: 火車誤點了 "the train is late", 班機誤點. It is the exact word for public transport running behind time. The reverse is 準點 "on time". 誤 "miss, delay" + 點 "point of time". Not used for people being late: that is 遲到.

column3: An idiom for being helpless, having no way out: 无可奈何地说 "said helplessly", 无可奈何的事 "something that cannot be helped". It is used as an adverb to describe how someone does something, with 地. It is made of 无 "no" + 可 "can" + 奈何 "do anything about". A shorter form is 无奈.
column4: 他无可奈何地点了点头。
column5: 他無可奈何地點了點頭。
column6: Tā wúkěnàihé de diǎn le diǎntóu.
column7: He nodded, having no alternative.
column9: An idiom for being helpless, having no way out: 無可奈何地說 "said helplessly", 無可奈何的事 "something that cannot be helped". It is used as an adverb to describe how someone does something, with 地. It is made of 無 "no" + 可 "can" + 奈何 "do anything about". A shorter form is 無奈.

column3: Physics as a subject, and "physical" in the sense of the natural: 物理老师, 物理课 "physics class", 物理现象 "physical phenomenon". 物 "matter, things" + 理 "principle", so it is the principles of things. 理 has 王 "jade" on the left, and in an older sense meant to polish jade along its grain.
column6: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan shàng wùlǐ kè.
column7: I like physics class best.
column9: Physics as a subject, and "physical" in the sense of the natural: 物理老師, 物理課 "physics class", 物理現象 "physical phenomenon". 物 "matter, things" + 理 "principle", so it is the principles of things. 理 has 王 "jade" on the left, and in an older sense meant to polish jade along its grain.

column3: Heartless, ruthless: 无情的人 "a heartless person", 无情无义 "no feeling, no loyalty", and also for forces, 无情的岁月 "cruel time". 无 "without" + 情 "feeling". The opposite is 多情 or 有情. 情 has 忄 "heart" on the left and 青 on the right, which still sounds close (qíng and qīng).
column6: Tā duì wǒ hěn wúqíng.
column7: He is heartless toward me.
column9: Heartless, ruthless: 無情的人 "a heartless person", 無情無義 "no feeling, no loyalty", and also for forces, 無情的歲月 "cruel time". 無 "without" + 情 "feeling". The opposite is 多情 or 有情. 情 has 忄 "heart" on the left and 青 on the right, which still sounds close (qíng and qīng).

column3: A dance hall or ballroom, a place for social dancing: 舞厅跳舞. It sounds a little old-fashioned today; a modern club is 夜店. 舞 "dance" + 厅 "hall". 厅 has 厂 above and 丁 on the inside, and the same 厅 ends 客厅 "living room" and 餐厅 "dining hall".
column4: 他们周末常去舞厅跳舞。
column5: 他們週末常去舞廳跳舞。
column6: Tāmen zhōumò cháng qù wǔtīng tiàowǔ.
column7: They often go dancing at the dance hall on weekends.
column9: A dance hall or ballroom, a place for social dancing: 舞廳跳舞. It sounds a little old-fashioned today; a modern club is 夜店. 舞 "dance" + 廳 "hall". 廳 has 广 "building" above and 聽 on the inside, and the same 廳 ends 客廳 "living room" and 餐廳 "dining hall".

column3: Not meaning to, or having no intention: 无意中 "without meaning to", 我无意伤害你 "I did not mean to hurt you". 无 "without" + 意 "intention". It is used in two ways: as "accidental" before 中 or before a verb, and as "have no wish to do" with a verb. 意 has 心 "heart" at the bottom, like most words for thought and wish.
column6: Wǒ wúyì shānghài nǐ.
column7: I had no intention of hurting you.
column9: Not meaning to, or having no intention: 無意中 "without meaning to", 我無意傷害你 "I did not mean to hurt you". 無 "without" + 意 "intention". It is used in two ways: as "accidental" before 中 or before a verb, and as "have no wish to do" with a verb. 意 has 心 "heart" at the bottom, like most words for thought and wish.

column3: Blind, and also "for no purpose, at random": 瞎了一只眼 "blind in one eye", 瞎说 "talk nonsense", 瞎忙 "busy for nothing". It is used for losing sight, and in speech for doing things without sense. 目 "eye" shows the meaning and 害 the sound (xiā and hài, which no longer sound very close).
column6: Tā de yī zhī yǎnjing xiā le.
column7: He is blind in one eye.
column9: Blind, and also "for no purpose, at random": 瞎了一隻眼 "blind in one eye", 瞎說 "talk nonsense", 瞎忙 "busy for nothing". It is used for losing sight, and in speech for doing things without sense. 目 "eye" shows the meaning and 害 the sound (xiā and hài, which no longer sound very close).

column3: Shrimp or prawn: 煮虾 "cook shrimp", 虾仁 "shelled shrimp", 大虾. 虾 has 虫 "insect" on its left, the part for small creatures and crustaceans (螃蟹), and 下 on the right for the sound.
column6: Wǒ zuì ài chī xiā.
column7: I love eating shrimp most.
column9: Shrimp or prawn: 煮蝦 "cook shrimp", 蝦仁 "shelled shrimp", 大蝦. 蝦 has 虫 "insect" on its left, the part for small creatures and crustaceans (螃蟹), and 叚 on the right for the sound.

column3: Shrimp, the spoken form with 子 on the end, as 桌子 and 椅子 do: 虾子 is the word for the animal or the meat. 虾 alone is more common in compounds and menus (虾仁, 虾饺). The ending 子 is a small noun suffix, and neutral in tone here.
column6: Xiāzi yào zhǔ shú le cái hǎochī.
column7: Shrimp are only tasty once they are well cooked.
column9: Shrimp, the spoken form with 子 on the end, as 桌子 and 椅子 do: 蝦子 is the word for the animal or the meat. 蝦 alone is more common in compounds and menus (蝦仁, 蝦餃). The ending 子 is a small noun suffix, and neutral in tone here.

column3: The chin: 下巴很尖 "a pointed chin", 摸下巴 "stroke one's chin", 双下巴 "double chin". 下 "lower" + 巴, where 巴 only gives the sound (bā) and a neutral tone in this word.
column6: Tā de xiàba shàng yǒu yī kē zhì.
column7: He has a mole on his chin.
column9: The chin: 下巴很尖 "a pointed chin", 摸下巴 "stroke one's chin", 雙下巴 "double chin". 下 "lower" + 巴, where 巴 only gives the sound (bā) and a neutral tone in this word.

column3: Taiwanese Hokkien-based slang for "what": 虾米 stands in for 什么 in casual talk, as in 你说虾米 "what are you saying". The characters are only a spelling of the sound of the Taiwanese words, so the meaning "shrimp" does not apply: the same two characters also name a small dried shrimp. Keep it for jokes and casual talk with friends, not formal speech.
column6: Nǐ gāngcái shuō xiāmǐ?
